title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section, 'Construction of expression vectors...' paragraph describing T0 and T2 transgenic screening
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'Among the T₀ putative transgenics (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m) hptII gene specific PCR positive plants were selected and advanced to next generation. Homozygous T₂ lines showing the presence of hptII gene at 1 kb, PcINO1 gene at 1.5 kb and PcIMT1 gene at 1.1 kb region respectively (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m) were selected for Southern blot analysis...' The identical supplementary figure range (S5g–m) is cited for two distinct experiments at two different generations (T0 PCR screening and T2 homozygous PCR confirmation) without any explanation of how the same figure panels represent both analyses, indicating a referencing inconsistency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section, Southern blot/segregation analysis paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states Southern blot analysis was performed on 'Homozygous T₂ lines' (110/153/98 plants for PcINO1/PcIMT1/DC1), but the very next sentence refers to 'Southern positive T₃ PcINO1-plants exhibiting additional single-copy integration...were used for segregation analysis,' introducing a generation (T3) that was not stated to have undergone the Southern blot procedure described immediately before, creating an unexplained generational inconsistency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section, 'Selected T4 plant lines...12 hrs salt stress' paragraph (Figure 5a,b description)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: '7PcINO1-line recorded a ~2.61 fold increase in the INO1 transcript under stress as against ~0.5 fold in 10PcIMT1 line and 0.67 fold in 6DC1 line under similar conditions.' Values of 0.5 and 0.67 (i.e., less than 1) represent a decrease relative to baseline, not an 'increase.' Framing all three values together as instances of 'fold increase' misrepresents the direction of change for the 10PcIMT1 and 6DC1 lines, which actually show a decrease in INO1 transcript under stress.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section, comparison between Fig. 5a,b and Fig. 5d descriptions for the 6DC1 line
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text reports that in the 6DC1 line under stress, total INO1 transcript (detected via the common OsINO1/PcINO1 probe) showed a 0.67-fold change (i.e., a decrease) (Fig. 5a,b), while the PcINO1-transgene-specific 37-amino-acid transcript in the same 6DC1 line under the same stress condition showed a ~5-fold increase (Fig. 5d). Since the PcINO1-specific transcript is a component of the total INO1 signal, a large increase in the transgene-specific fraction alongside a net decrease in total transcript is not reconciled or explained in the text, representing an unaddressed internal contradiction in the reported transcript trends for the same line and condition.

The abstract concludes that 'The PcIMT1-lines or the double transgenic lines (DC1) having PcINO1 and PcIMT1 introgressed together, were less efficient' at conferring salt tolerance compared to PcINO1 lines. However, the Results explicitly identify one top-performing line from each transgenic type (7PcINO1, 10PcIMT1, and 6DC1) as collectively 'the best in terms of growth parameters' (Fig. 3a-c), showing comparable maximal root growth (Fig. 3d-f), and all three 'fully recovered their normal physiological activity' after 300 mM stress for 10 days and recovered best after 15 days of stress withdrawal (Fig. 4a-h). This detailed data showing comparable performance among top lines from all three genotype categories is in tension with the abstract's blanket claim that PcIMT1 and DC1 lines are categorically 'less efficient.'
